title: Navaratri: nine nights of the Goddess
hookLine: Durga meets the buffalo demon; nine nights of dancing, and on the tenth day the good wins
carry: durga: the power of every god, as mother
last: GOD HAS A FORM, AND IS BEYOND IT.

lines: A TEN-ARMED GODDESS ON A LION.
cards: Eleven at night in Gujarat, and an open ground is packed. People in mirrored skirts and embroidered jackets move in huge circles, clapping, spinning, sticks clicking in rhythm.
They'll be back tomorrow night, and the night after: nine nights in a row. Far to the east, in Bengal, neighborhoods build glittering temporary halls for a ten-armed goddess on a lion.

In the south, families set out steps of dolls. Different places, different customs, the same nine nights. And at the center of many of them, one story: a demon nobody could defeat, and the Goddess who did.

teach.h: THE GODS' LIGHT BECOMES THE GODDESS.
teach.b: The story comes from the Devi Mahatmya, the Glory of the Goddess, a Sanskrit text recited in homes and temples during these nights.
Mahishasura, a demon who is part buffalo, grows so powerful that he drives the gods out of heaven.
The gods are so furious that their anger bursts out of them as light, and the light of every god flows together into one blazing form: a woman. The Goddess.
Each god hands her a weapon: Shiva's trident, Vishnu's discus, and a lion to ride. People call her Durga, the one who is hard to reach, hard to defeat. She rides out laughing.
Mahishasura keeps changing shape to escape her: a buffalo, a lion, a warrior with a sword, an elephant, a buffalo again.

teach.h: DURGA MEETS EVERY FORM HE TAKES.
teach.b: She meets every form, and as he struggles half out of the buffalo's body, she ends it. That's why images of Durga so often show her spear in a buffalo. Now the teaching.

teach.h: SHAKTI: GOD AS MOTHER, THE POWER OF ALL.
teach.b: She is all their power in one: Shakti, God as Mother, the power behind everything that moves. What no single god could do, she does.
Many teachers read the buffalo as the stubborn, dull part of us that keeps changing disguise, and these nights as asking the Mother to meet it.
Navaratri: nava, nine, and ratri, night.

teach.h: DURGA: THE POWER OF EVERY GOD, AS MOTHER.
teach.b: Some honor nine forms of the Goddess, one each night. Some dance the garba for her. The tenth day, Vijayadashami, is the day of victory; in much of north India it's also Dussehra, for Rama's victory over Ravana.

how: During Navaratri, Hindus honor the Goddess over nine nights in regional ways: garba and dandiya dancing in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal, displays of dolls (golu) in the south, fasting and recitation of the Devi Mahatmya in many homes; the tenth day, Vijayadashami or Dussehra, celebrates the victory of good.

o: nine days of silence before a wedding
a pilgrimage to nine river temples

games.q: what's inside the festival — tap the pairs.
p: born from the light of all the gods
God as Mother, the power of all

s: Navaratri is celebrated the same way everywhere
garba in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal, dolls in the south, and much more.
in the story, Durga is formed from the light of all the gods together
she isn't their helper: she's Shakti, the power of every god in one, worshipped as Mother.
in much of north India it also celebrates Rama's victory over Ravana.

games.q: you're Durga. the demon you're fighting keeps changing shape: buffalo, lion, warrior, elephant. what do you do?
o: wait until he tires himself out.
call the gods back to help.
games.why: she meets every form, and ends it as he struggles half out of the buffalo's body. that's why her spear is in a buffalo in so many images.

practice: Many families light a lamp for the Goddess on each of these nights. If you pray, light one, or picture one, and say Jai Mata Di, victory to the Mother, or simply, Ma.

Then name one thing that keeps changing shape on you: the urge to snap, the voice that says you're not enough. Ask for her strength to meet it, just tonight. If you don't pray, name it, and decide: not tonight.

wordCard.voice: Navaratri. Nava, nine; ratri, night. Nine nights of the Goddess, and on the tenth day, victory.

carryVoice: Your line: durga, the power of every god, as mother. What no one god could do, she did. See you tomorrow.
